title: URDF Overview - Unified Robot Description Format
description:
The Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) is an XML format used in ROS to describe all aspects of a robot. It's a foundational tool for representing a robot's physical structure, visual properties, and inertial characteristics. Understanding URDF is crucial for simulating robots, performing motion planning, and visualizing robot models in tools like Rviz.

## 1. Why URDF?

URDF provides a standardized, human-readable way to describe a robot. Its key benefits include A common format for robot descriptions across the ROS ecosystem.
   Visualization Enables simulation environments (e.g., Gazebo) to load robot models and simulate their physics.
   Motion Planning Robot descriptions can be built from smaller, reusable components.

## 2. Core Concepts A link represents a rigid body of the robot. This could be a robot arm segment, a wheel, the base, or any other physical part that moves as a single unit.

### Joints

   Definition URDF supports several joint types, each allowing different degrees of freedom A rotational joint around a single axis (e.g., a hinge, a robot arm joint).
       continuous A translational joint along a single axis (e.g., a linear slide).
       fixed A 6-DOF joint, typically used for the base link of a robot to represent its movement in 3D space.
       planar Each non-root joint connects a parent link to a child link. The motion of the child link is defined relative to its parent.

Example of a Joint in URDF Simplifying URDF

Writing complex robot descriptions purely in URDF can be verbose and repetitive. Xacro (XML Macros) is a preprocessor for URDF that allows for Define reusable blocks of XML that can be instantiated multiple times.
   Variables Perform calculations within the XML.

Xacro greatly simplifies the creation and maintenance of complex URDF files. A typical workflow involves writing robot descriptions in Xacro (.urdf.xacro files) and then converting them to standard URDF (.urdf` files) for consumption by ROS 2 tools.

## Conclusion

URDF is the standard language for describing robots in ROS 2, providing a rich framework for defining a robot's physical structure, visuals, and dynamics through links and joints. Coupled with Xacro for enhanced readability and reusability, URDF forms the foundation for robot simulation, visualization, and advanced motion planning in robotics applications.
